workedExamples.title: Mean vs. median — they are usually different

steps.prompt: We have the data set 3, 5, 7, 8, 12. First, what is the mean? Add the values and divide by how many there are.
steps.reveal: Sum = 3+5+7+8+12 = 35. There are 5 values, so mean = 35 / 5 = 7.

steps.prompt: Now find the median. Put the values in order and find the middle one.
steps.reveal: Already in order: 3, 5, 7, 8, 12. With 5 values the middle (3rd) value is 7. Median = 7. Here they happen to be equal.

steps.prompt: Change one value: use 3, 5, 7, 8, 22 instead. Recompute the mean.

steps.reveal: Middle value is still 7. Median = 7, but the mean is now 9 — they are different.

steps.prompt: What is the lesson about mean and median?
steps.reveal: Mean and median are NOT the same number in general. The mean uses every value's size; the median only cares about position. Never assume the middle of a list equals its average.

workedExamples.title: An outlier moves the mean but barely moves the median

steps.prompt: Start with 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. Find the mean and the median.
steps.reveal: Sum = 10+12+14+16+18 = 70, mean = 70 / 5 = 14. Median is the middle value = 14.

steps.prompt: Now add an outlier so the data is 10, 12, 14, 16, 48. Recompute the mean.
steps.reveal: Sum = 10+12+14+16+48 = 100, mean = 100 / 5 = 20. The mean jumped from 14 to 20.
Order: 10, 12, 14, 16, 48. Middle value = 14. Median is still 14.

steps.prompt: Compare how far each measure moved.
steps.reveal: The mean moved 6 (from 14 to 20). The median did not move at all (14 to 14). The outlier pulled the mean toward itself but left the median alone.
The MEDIAN is resistant — outliers barely affect it. The MEAN is sensitive — one extreme value can change it a lot. Use the median to describe a center when outliers are present.
